system.name: mRPC
system.one_liner: an RPC framework that runs marshalling and policy enforcement as a single privileged, managed system service instead of a library plus sidecar

components.name: Stub
components.role: compiled protocol stub the app is built with

components.name: mRPC Library
components.role: library apps use to build against mRPC and, at runtime, to allocate and dispatch RPCs via shared memory

components.name: mRPC Schema Compiler
components.role: compiles a Proto definition into the stub used by the app

components.name: Proto
components.role: the protocol/interface definition supplied by the developer

components.name: Proto Codegen
components.role: generates app-specific marshalling code inside the mRPC service

components.name: libApp
components.role: app-specific marshalling library compiled and loaded into both the app and the mRPC service

components.name: Shared Memory
components.role: control and data region used to pass RPC requests/responses between the app and mRPC with minimal copies

components.name: RPC Engines
components.role: runtime engines inside mRPC that process dispatched RPCs

components.name: Frontend
components.role: engine that routes RPCs and applies policy at runtime

components.name: Policy
components.role: policy enforcement stage inside the RPC processing pipeline

components.name: Global QoS Policy
components.role: policy operators apply globally or per-app across the mRPC service

components.name: RDMA
components.role: transport backend an operator can update

components.name: TCP
components.role: transport backend an operator can update

flows.what: protocol definition compiled into a stub
Connect(Proto, ...) request specifying protocols of interest
compile and load app-specific marshalling library
RPC request allocated and dispatched via shared memory (key/meta/data)
dispatched RPC handed to RPC engines
processed RPC forwarded through Policy and RDMA/libApp to the network
operator applies/updates policy without modifying the app

content.key_idea: mRPC's workflow spans three phases: users build and connect apps against the service using a compiled stub (initialization), invoke RPCs that are dispatched through shared memory with minimal copying (runtime), and operators apply or update global/per-app policies without touching application code (management).
content.reading_order: left to right across three columns—User-Initialization, User-Runtime, Operator-Management—following the circled step numbers 1 through 7 within each column.

evidence: Figure 2 shows a high-level overview of the mRPC architecture and workflow, breaking it down into three major phases: initialization, runtime, and management
The mRPC service runs as a non-root, user-space process with access to the necessary network devices and a shared-memory region for each application
The initialization phase extends from building the applica- tion to how the application binds to a specific RPC interface

summary: This figure walks through mRPC's end-to-end workflow in three side-by-side phases. In User-Initialization, an app is built with the mRPC library and a compiled stub, connects to the mRPC service specifying a Proto of interest, and mRPC compiles and loads an app-specific marshalling library. In User-Runtime, the app invokes RPCs through familiar stubs; the mRPC library allocates and dispatches requests via a shared-memory region, and the mRPC service's Frontend, Policy, and RDMA/libApp stages process the RPC with minimal copying. In Operator-Management, operators apply or update a Global QoS Policy and transport backends (RDMA/TCP) across multiple apps (A, B, C) without disrupting or modifying any application code. Circled numbers 1-7 mark the sequence within and across the three phases.
summary_zh: 该图分三个阶段展示mRPC工作流：用户初始化阶段构建并连接应用；用户运行时阶段通过共享内存分发RPC并由mRPC处理；运营管理阶段中运维人员可全局或按应用更新策略而无需改动应用代码。
